t:
(a) Mandatory Possession or Wear Date.—The Secretary of the Navy shall change the mandatory possession or wear date of the alternate combination cover or the unisex combination cover from October 31, 2016, to October 31, 2018. 
    (b) Evaluation and Report.—Not later than February 1, 2017, the Secretary of the Navy shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives a report on the evaluation of the Navy female service dress uniforms based on surveying a representative group of female officer and enlisted service members. Such evaluation shall include each of the following:
        (1) An identification of the operational need addressed by the alternate combination cover or the unisex combination cover. 
        (2) An assessment of the individual cost of service dress uniform items to members of the Armed Forces as a percentage of their monthly pay. 
        (3) The composition of each uniform item’s wear test group. 
        (4) An identification of the costs to the Navy and to individual members of the Armed Forces for uniform changes identified in the Navy administrative message 236/15 dated October 9, 2015. 
        (5) The opinions of a representative group of female officer and enlisted service members of the Navy active and reserve components. 
        (6) Any other rationale the Secretary determines appropriate.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that surveying a representative group and gathering their opinions amounts to public consultation. However, those surveyed are Navy officer and enlisted service members, who are federal personnel inside the government, and the survey feeds a report to congressional committees, which are also inside the government. No state, tribe, company, outside expert, or member of the general public is brought into a federal decision, and no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: the Secretary of the Navy shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives a report on the evaluation of the Navy female service dress uniforms based on surveying a representative group of female officer and enlisted service members

opus.w: The only people consulted are active and reserve Navy service members, who are federal personnel. The results go into a report to congressional committees, and Congress is also inside the federal government. The survey looks like outside input, but it never crosses the federal boundary. It also feeds a report rather than a federal decision, and no comment period, hearing, outside advisory body or right to sue is created.
opus.s: the Secretary of the Navy shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives a report on the evaluation of the Navy female service dress uniforms based on surveying a representative group of female officer and enlisted service members
opus.b:
I labelled this **No**: everyone involved is inside the federal government.

**Tempting reading:** The section requires a survey of "a representative group of female officer and enlisted service members" and asks for their opinions. That looks like gathering stakeholder input.

**Why it fails:** Navy service members are federal personnel. The survey also only feeds a report to the congressional Armed Services Committees, and Congress is inside the federal government too. Subsection (a), which changes the wear date, involves no outside party at all.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of the Navy to submit a report to Congress based on a survey of Navy service members. Both the recipients of the report (Congress) and the subjects of the survey (Navy officers and enlisted members) are inside the federal government. The definition states that consultation or coordination between federal agencies or with federal employees is not participation. There is no involvement of outside parties such as the general public, states, or non-federal experts in the decision-making process described.
qwen_chat.s: submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives a report on the evaluation of the Navy female service dress uniforms based on surveying a representative group of female officer and enlisted service members
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "surveying a representative group of female officer and enlisted service members" constitutes participation because it involves gathering opinions from people. However, these service members are federal employees (inside the government), and the definition explicitly states that if every actor involved is inside the federal government, the answer is "No". Furthermore, the survey is for an internal evaluation/report to Congress, not a public comment period or advisory board with outside members.
